name: Ultium Cells - Lordstown (Warren), OH
type: Battery Cell Plant (GM / LG Energy Solution JV)

fieldNotes.facility: Positively identified as the Ultium Cells Lordstown battery cell plant (GM / LG Energy Solution JV), the ~2.8M sq ft, ~156-acre cell-manufacturing facility off Tod Ave SW / Ohltown Rd in Lordstown (mailing city Warren), OH. The roster address 2440 Ohltown Rd geocodes to a residential subdivision ~2.5 km NE; re-pinned to the large white-roof plant building at ~41.1538,-80.8635, immediately east of the former GM Lordstown Assembly complex and its rail yard. Confirmed by Ultium / GM / GMAuthority sources (156 acres, 2.8M+ sq ft, ~30 GWh, production since Aug 2022, >100M cells produced by late 2024).
fieldNotes.geofence: Perimeter traces the developed/fenced plant parcel: the main plant building runs roughly N-S with a slight rotation; the ring also captures the west-side process/utility yards, the SE employee parking field, the south staging/laydown area, and retention ponds. ~156 acres consistent with published site size.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Marked true (medium confidence). The plant frontage on public Ohltown Rd (E side) is open grass/field with no public truck approach (2025-07 Street View shows the building set far back across an open field). Truck circulation enters from the SW/south via internal Lordstown-complex roads to a fenced, controlled gate near the SW corner of the building. A secured battery-cell campus (valuable IP, lithium hazmat) operates controlled gated access; exact gate hardware not crisply resolved from overhead, so flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true (medium confidence). A small gatehouse-footprint structure consistent with a staffed booth sits at the SW truck approach; standard for a GM/LG JV cell plant of this security profile. Not positively resolved as a booth, so flagged; remoteGs false as a consequence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 25-50 (count ~35). A single principal material-handling dock bank runs along the SOUTH face of the building with trailers and intermodal containers (orange/blue/white) backed in (sgate/sdock/swdock z18 imagery). No second large dock bank on a separate face was resolved, so shipRcvSeparate left false (flagged).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Banded 10-25. Trailers and containers are staged/dropped on the south apron and SW corner lots without tractors; a dedicated trailer-storage row is present (dropYard true). Much surrounding flat ground is contractor laydown/expansion area rather than marked trailer stalls.
fieldNotes.dropYard: True — dedicated trailer/container drop area on the south apron separate from active dock positions.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: True — deep paved aprons and perimeter loop road inside the fence before the dock face provide internal staging/queue space.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: True — the internal approach from the SW gate to the south dock face is long and can hold a multi-truck queue without spilling to a public road; backupSensitive false (gate is internal, far from public Ohltown Rd).
fieldNotes.railServed: Marked true (flagged). An extensive multi-track rail yard (former GM Lordstown Assembly yard) sits immediately NW of the plant, and a rail line runs the wooded corridor along the west property edge; the complex is rail-served. A spur running directly into the Ultium cell building was not positively confirmed from imagery, so flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Counted 2 — the single large plant building dominates; a smaller separate ancillary/process building sits to the south near the entrance. Functionally one integrated plant, so multipleFacilities false.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: True — wide paved aprons and surplus graded width around the SW entrance and south loop road leave ample room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Approximate (~2 in / 1 out) from overhead; low confidence — flagged.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh pad positively identified; left false and flagged.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Lordstown is a small rural township; the plant is surrounded by farmland, woods, and the low-density Lordstown industrial corridor. Rural.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: False — rural but immediately adjacent to a major active industrial complex with strong infrastructure and transmission corridors; cellular coverage expected adequate.

citations.claim: Lordstown is a GM / LG Energy Solution joint venture operated by Ultium Cells LLC; GM states the Lansing-stake sale 'does not change GM's ownership interest in Ultium Cells and does not affect joint venture plans at the battery plants in Spring Hill and Lordstown'
GM and LG Energy Solution jointly invested $2.3B to build the Lordstown OH cell plant under the Ultium Cells joint venture

verification.rationale: REJECTED per the 'JV the account does not operate' rule: the Lordstown cell plant is operated by Ultium Cells LLC, a separate GM / LG Energy Solution joint-venture operating company, not GM directly. (Site remains an active Ultium JV plant as of late 2025 despite EV-related layoffs; GM retains its Lordstown JV stake.)
